what_it_is.prose: International Aero Engines (IAE AG) is a multinational aero-engine consortium — led by Pratt & Whitney (RTX) with MTU Aero Engines, Japanese Aero Engines Corporation and other partners — that develops and produces the V2500 turbofan, one of the most widely produced commercial engines (best known on the Airbus A320ceo family, with over 300 million flight hours in service). In the military-transport context, two V2500 engines power the Embraer C-390 Millennium / KC-390. India's only relevance to IAE is prospective: the C-390 is a leading contender in the Indian Air Force's roughly ₹1-lakh-crore Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) tender, and long-term V2500 engine support has been cited as a factor in that competition. IAE has no engines in Indian military service, no Indian order and no Indian industrial partner. This dossier is deliberately a short Tier C stub: it records the absence of an IAE India footprint honestly rather than inferring one from the C-390's tender candidacy.
